title: Less Information, More Comparison, and Better Performance: Evidence from a Field Experiment

scopes.description: Full supplied main-analysis workflow for reported Tables 2–9, starting from the author-prepared LIMC Data.dta panel and retaining every supplied analysis branch. The historical raw-source compilation is recorded as conditional lineage because LIMC Code.do consumes the prepared panel directly.

issues.description: LIMC Data.dta is the direct Table 2–9 input but is absent from the package inventory. The authors describe a compiled master panel; the source code uses that panel directly. Its actual columns, types, participant-ID structure, round coverage and current authorized route are unverified. The six SportsTec exports and QuestBack survey are historical lineage and a conditional alternative only; their raw files and compilation recipe are not supplied. No private eligibility check or contact was made. Frozen catalog discovery returned no matching product candidate, while unrelated lexical hits do not establish an access barrier or absence of other routes.
The input and all eight table exports use absolute paths from the authors' machine; configure a working-copy input/output root and update the input and every table destination consistently.

The supplied Stata 18 load line ends with replace. The Stata 18 User's Guide presents clear for accepting loss of unsaved in-memory data during use and describes replace as saving over an existing dataset; the current official use syntax lists clear and nolabel. This is a supported narrow source correction, not an execution-tested diagnosis.

If raw-source construction is the only route, obtain the missing producer/field/merge/exclusion specification and establish authorized access to both the six SportsTec exports and QuestBack survey inputs; do not infer eligibility or reconstruct the panel from the datasheet alone.
validation: After an authorized compatible panel is staged, verify its actual columns and round coverage before a separately authorized Table 2–9 run.

Apply all nine line replacements shown above together in a working copy: line 18 plus each of the eight table exports. Keep the original source untouched and retain all analysis commands.
Use the Stata host wrapper in batch mode with relative paths; before any separately authorized run, verify the wrapper sees the chosen working directory and can write the tables directory.

review_notes: Dependency closure is established for the supplied main-analysis code: the sole frozen read edge is mapped to R_MASTER, direct fields and generated-variable handoffs are traced, and all eight Table 2–9 output calls are accounted for. Panel access, actual schema and round coverage remain unresolved, so execution readiness is undetermined.

The static-audit scanner reports eight missing exports, but direct inspection of all 301 source lines shows an esttab export for each supplied table. The audit is retained as discovery evidence and its export finding is not treated as an outcome.

The prepared LIMC Data.dta panel is the sole primary data requirement. Six SportsTec exports and QuestBack survey data remain conditional historical lineage, not separate mandatory AND requirements while a compatible prepared-panel route is possible.

An initial saved resource-checkpoint helper failed with a missing local variable; its exact source and captured diagnostic are preserved under probes, and a versioned correction produced this checkpoint. No scientific interpretation or author source was changed by that construction failure.
No author code, estimator, or empirical dataset was executed or imported; no data were downloaded, no packages installed, and no source edits applied.
